candidates.name: National History Museum
candidates.content: The largest museum in Albania holds many of the country's archaeological treasures and a replica of Skanderbeg's massive sword (how he held it, rode his horse and fought at the same time, is a mystery). The lighting might be poor

candidates.name: National Gallery of Arts
candidates.content: Tracing the relatively brief history of Albanian painting from the early 19th century to the present day, this beautiful space also has temporary exhibitions. The interesting collection includes 19th-century paintings depicting sc

candidates.name: National Archaeological Museum
candidates.content: Features ancient artifacts from Illyrian to Roman and Hellenic times: wonderful mosaics, Roman statues and illustrative maps. The collection here is comprehensive and impressive in parts, but there's only minimal labelling in Alba

candidates.name: Bunk'Art
candidates.content: This fantastic conversion, from a massive cold war bunker on the outskirts of Tirana into a history and contemporary art museum, is easily a Tirana highlight. With almost 3,000 m² of space underground spread over several floors, t

candidates.name: Bunk'Art 2
candidates.content: The little cousin to the main Bunk'art, this museum, which is within a communist-era bunker and underground tunnel system below the ministry of Interior Affairs, focuses on the role of the police and security services in Albania t

candidates.name: House of Leaves
candidates.content: This grand old 1930s building started life as Albania's first maternity hospital, but within a few years the focus turned from creating new lives to ending lives as the hospital was converted to an interrogation and surveillance c

candidates.name: The Museum of the Bank of Albania
candidates.content: The museum lies on two floors, each of which is conceived as an independent space from the other. On the first floor is presented the rich numismatic collection of the Bank of Albania from antiquity to the present day. The second

candidates.name: Clock Tower
candidates.content: This tower has become a symbol of Tirana. It is one of the oldest constructions in Tirana, built in the 1820s. Don't forget to visit the nearby Clock Towers of Albania Museum featuring Clock Towers from around Albania, and traditi

candidates.name: Petrela Castle
candidates.alt: Petrelë Castle, Albanian: Kalaja e Petrelës
candidates.content: This is one of Albania's best-preserved castles. It is known as an ancient settlement 2000 years old and was commanded by princess Mamica, the sister of the national hero, Skanderbeg.

candidates.name: Tirana Mosaic
candidates.content: The mosaic was discovered following excavations for an apartment complex. Various artifacts point to the presence of a village in the area thousands of years ago. This is the only archaeological site in Tirana.

candidates.name: Fortress of Justinian (Tirana Castle remains)
candidates.alt: Albanian: Kalaja e Justinianit, Kalaja e Tiranës
candidates.content: The history of this castle in dates back before 1300 and is a remnant from the Byzantine-era. The fortress is the place where the main east-west and north-south roads crossed, and formed the heart of Tirana. About all that's left

candidates.name: Piramid
candidates.content: Completely renovated and reopened in May 2023, the pyramid was built in 1987 according to the design of Enver Hoxha's daughter and was opened as a museum dedicated to her father. In 2007 US President George W. Bush gave a speech i

candidates.name: Saint Paul Catholic Cathedral
candidates.content: This modern cathedral features fascinating window murals.

candidates.name: Resurrection of Christ Orthodox Cathedral
candidates.alt: Katedralja Ortodokse e Ringjalljes se Krishtit, Katedralja "Ngjallja e Krishtit" ne Tirane
candidates.content: This cathedral features fascinating architecture and rich interior iconography. The church covered with a 23-m-high dome

candidates.name: Natural Sciences Museum of Albania
candidates.content: This museum features the fauna and geological composition of Albania.

candidates.name: Tirana Zoo
candidates.content: Visiting this zoo is an odd experience; there are few animals but you will see them at remarkably close range. Nearby is the Botanical Garden featuring the best of Albania's fauna.

candidates.name: Preze Castle
candidates.content: This 15th-century castle is on the picturesque hills of Preze village west of Rinas airport.

candidates.name: Dajti Castle ruins
candidates.content: An archaeological site comprising the remains of a Roman fortification (built over an earlier Illyrian castle) on a mountainside of Mount Dajti.

candidates.name: Et'hem Bey Mosque
candidates.content: Construction of this mosque took about 28 years and finished in 1821. It is considered one of the most beautiful mosques in Albania with very interesting decorations and artwork within it. Reopened in 2021 after full restoration.

candidates.name: Mosque 'Kokonozit'
candidates.content: Finished in 1750 during Ottoman rule and one of the few that survived the Communist rule intact. During that time the building functioned as a storehouse and a tobacco shop, then in 1991 it was returned to its original use.

candidates.name: Kapllan Pasha Tomb
candidates.content: Built in 1820, originally next to a mosque which was destroyed during WWII. Kapllan Pasha was an Ottoman ruler of Tirana who was buried here, but his remains were later moved to Istanbul.

candidates.name: The Sheh Dyrri Teqe
candidates.content: This is a teqe (teqe or cemevi is a Turkish meeting house for communal worship service) in Tirana. Back in the day it was also the home of a local sheikh. It's listed as a cultural monument of Albania, however it's private propert

candidates.name: Tanners' Mosque
candidates.content: Built in the 17th century in a part of the city where leather workers lived. It was largely destroyed by a lightning strike in 1927, but quickly rebuilt. Functioning as a storehouse during the Communist rule, in 1990 it was renova

candidates.name: ZETA Center for Contemporary Art
candidates.content: As non-profit exhibition space founded in 2007. With its 150 m² area on the second floor of a mixed residential and commercial building at Abdyl Frashëri Street No.7 in the Blloku area of Tirana (zona Libri Universitar: between Sa

candidates.name: Historical Museum of the Armed Forces
candidates.content: This museum contains more than a thousand objects, from the Middle Ages to the 19th century, decorated with gold and silver, a range of display cases with rifles of various types of Medieval, Renaissance, Skanderbeg's swords, of A

candidates.name: Studio House "Kadare"
candidates.price: Adult 500 lek, family (two or more persons) 250 lek, student 80 lek
candidates.content: This apartment was the residence of Kadare, an important writer, from 1974 to 1989, and his work place. It was designed by architect Maks Velo in 1972, was declared category II Culture Monument in 2015. The modernist and cubist bu

candidates.name: Blloku or Ish-Blloku
candidates.content: Among the apartment blocks, one can find some of Tirana's trendiest cafés, shops, and restaurants. Here is also located the villa of the former dictator, Enver Hoxha. During communism, the area was reserved solely for government o

candidates.name: Tanners' Bridge
candidates.alt: Tabak Bridge, Albanian: Ura e Tabakëve
candidates.content: This is an 18th-century Ottoman period stone footbridge. The bridge was once part of the Shëngjergj Road that linked Tirana with the eastern highlands. The Shëngjergj Road furnished the city with agricultural produce and livestock

candidates.name: Mount Dajti National Park & Cable Car
candidates.content: The most accessible mountain in the country, and many locals go there to escape the city rush and have a spit-roast lamb lunch. A sky-high, Austrian-made cable car, Dajti Express, takes 15 minutes to make the scenic trip (almost)

candidates.name: Stroll along Bulevardi Dëshmorët e Kombit
candidates.content: A panoramic boulevard built by the Italians in the 1930s similar to the Champs de Elysee extending south from Skanderberg Square. The boulevard features Fascist, Communist, and modern architecture of government buildings, business

candidates.name: Taiwan Complex
candidates.content: This beautiful place in the heart of downtown Tirana. It includes restaurants, casinos, bars, a club, etc. It is surrounded by a huge lit water fountain with a glowing bridge that reaches to the restaurant, and is an ideal place f

candidates.name: Mother Teresa Square
candidates.content: Located at the southern side of Deshmoret e Kombit Boulevard, this square features typical fascist architecture. Buildings include the University of Tirana, Archaeological Institute, Academy of Arts and the National Stadium.

candidates.name: Grand Park along the Artificial Lake
candidates.content: People have picnics and have fun, and the natural beauty allows it because of the huge trees, open spaces, and mountains surrounding them. An artificial lake lies in the middle of the Park. It is popular with locals and tourists a

candidates.name: Tirana International Film Festival
candidates.content: This annual film festival held at the end of November and beginning of December highlights the work of ethnic Albanian artists.

candidates.name: Sheshi Skënderbej
candidates.content: Tirana's city centre. A statue of Albanian hero Skanderbeg stands in the square with the Albanian flag on the side. Renovations have made the square pedestrians and public transportation friendly. Government buildings featuring It

candidates.name: Ali Demi Skate Park
candidates.content: The Ali-Demi skate park is a great place to go with your family because there is a nice park on one of the sides next to the skate park, there are markets, and a beautiful café shop with a playground for small children with typica

candidates.name: Southeast of Tirana
candidates.content: There are many small resorts and restaurants in Tirana's greenbelt areas of Berzhite, Petrela, and Farke along Rruga e Elbasanit and SH3. One locality features shooting range facilities, a modest golf club and horse riding, while

candidates.name: Dajti Mini Golf
candidates.price: Child 2-4 €2, child 5-11 €7, adult 12+ €10, family of 4 (2 adults & 2 children) €28, discounted combo tickets can also be purchased at lower station
candidates.content: A fun mini-golf course, the only 18-hole course in the country. Suitable for players of all ages and with no previous experience needed. With a number of obstacles in your way, the aim of the game is to get your ball into the hole

candidates.name: Murat Toptani Street
candidates.content: Murat Toptani Street is a pedestrian-only street east of Rinia Park constructed with stone near the Tirana Castle walls. Traditional houses, cafes, and a local park are found here.

candidates.name: Brar Canyon and Bridge
candidates.content: A panoramic canyon and Ottoman bridge just steps from the capital. Spectacular views of the surrounding mountains and Tirana. A cave and a beautiful waterfall is found near Shengjergj village.

candidates.name: Lalzi Bay Beach
candidates.content: Popular weekend beach retreat where small seaside resorts can be found. This is also where Albania's wealthy rest. Visit Skanderbeg Castle along the cost, and a small church at Rodon Cape nearby.

candidates.name: General's Beach
candidates.content: A popular seaside weekend retreat. The name stems from an Italian general who used to rest at this beach during World War II. Accommodation is available in form of wooden villas. An international resort is also being build nearby

candidates.name: Rally Albania
candidates.content: The event features an international competition in the rough Albanian countryside roads.

candidates.name: Hemingway
candidates.content: A cocktail bar with Jazz, Blues, Reggae, etc. They also have inexpensive local beer, but they do not advertise it. Their service is not the quickest though.

candidates.name: Komiteti Kafe Muzeum
candidates.content: Styled as a cafe museum, this little bohemian place looks like a flea market. Every spare centimetre is crammed with communist-era relics, farming implements (those pitchforks hanging from the bar are probably a warning), Japanese

candidates.name: Old House Bar
candidates.content: The waiter isn't particular helpful and they just have beer and cocktails, no raki. But the crowd and place itself is worth a visit.

candidates.name: Radio
candidates.content: Named for the owner's collection of antique radios, deep-1950s lamp shades and even a collection of communist-era propaganda books to read over a cocktail. It attracts a young and well-fed crowd.

candidates.name: Tunel
candidates.content: Decent bar and club, with sometimes international DJs. In summer rooftop, in winter basement. They won't go longer than 02:00 or 03:00.

candidates.name: Hotspot Tirana
candidates.content: A coworking space, gallery, and sometimes club with open and friendly people. A very unlike-Albanian place.

candidates.name: Miqtë e Muzikës Live
candidates.content: A energetic place with live music (Jazz, regional) and a cordial host. Some people find it to be a tourist trap, so better ask for prices beforehand.

candidates.name: Sky Tower Rotating Bar
candidates.content: A bar in a rotating tower. The rotation is a bit jerky and may leave you slightly seasick.

candidates.name: Nektar Bookcafe
candidates.content: Supposedly one of the best salep of Albania can be found here.

candidates.name: My Way
candidates.content: Young locals and some expats frequent this cosy place.

candidates.name: My House
candidates.content: A little smokey inside but very local.

candidates.name: Oda
candidates.content: This restaurant inside a Tirana traditional house serves delicious traditional cuisine. Note that this is the original one — Oda Garden (aka ODS) south of Pazari is the hostile take-over one.

candidates.name: Chinese Garden
candidates.content: Sit-down, table-service Chinese restaurant, serving the western-versions of Chinese food, though one will occasionally see Chinese diplomats, businesspeople and tourists eating. Good food, large portions for the main dishes, noodl

candidates.name: Flower's
candidates.content: Daily menu and à-la-carte. Free water and bread as locals are used to it. Muzaka, creamy egg plant ... feels like the try beyond the usual.

candidates.name: Tasty
candidates.content: An authentic and plain cantine-like restaurant with a great choice of inexpensive, genuine Albanian dishes.

candidates.name: Te Dhuri
candidates.content: Only daily lunch menu available, no à-la-carte. Simple but delicious. Though, it seems a little Albanian might be needed to communicate your needs.

candidates.name: Vjosa
candidates.content: Serves all regular Albanian dishes; Supe Pule, Tashqebab, Tave Dheu, Salate Fshati, Fergese, etc.

candidates.name: Marion Restaurant
candidates.content: Budget self-service restaurant in the Central Campus. Very popular among students.

candidates.name: Tek Zgara Tirones 2
candidates.content: Good traditional Albanian cuisine with massive servings.

candidates.name: Birrari Ke Tori
candidates.content: Straightforward traditional Albanian food, with mostly meat dishes on the menu. The restaurant is practically in the basement, so it is easy to miss.

candidates.name: Gjelltore Dibra
candidates.content: Local dishes and central location.

candidates.name: Mr. Chicken
candidates.content: Good taste of Albanian fast food. Fresh rotisserie chicken

candidates.name: Gjiro Kamara fast food restaurant
candidates.content: Good taste of Albanian fast food.

candidates.name: Central Market
candidates.content: Rather touristic, so the prices are inflated. They have fresh fruit and vegetables, nuts, beans, flea market stuff, as well as traditional cooking utensils.

candidates.name: Fruit & Vegetables Market
candidates.content: Local produces and prices. There are also many stalls and shops towards it, having a similar variety, especially along Vath Koreshi (which also includes butchers).

candidates.name: Grand Bazaar
candidates.content: Fruits, vegetables, books, ceramics, 2nd-hand, kitchen appliances, cloths, shoes, etc. Bigger than the Central Market, non-touristy, but a little off-track.

candidates.name: Flea market
candidates.content: This certainly is a proper flea market, even though its style might deter most non-Albanians. It all looks dirty and is spread across the ground. Nevertheless, some good bargains and properly functioning things can be found here;

candidates.name: Fruit & Vegetables Popup Markets
candidates.content: There seem to exist some by the city sponsored markets that pop up from time to time. Though, no real time table is available. There is near Hemingway Bar.

december.text: Sulejman Pasha Bargjini, a native feudal lord from Mullet, established the city in 1614. His first constructions were a mosque, a bakery and a hamam or Turkish bath. On 8 February 1920, Tirana was made the temporary capital by the Congress of Lushnje, and it was proclaimed the permanent capital on 31 December 1925.

Albanians are very hospitable towards foreigners, despite media frequently portraying them unfairly as thieves and mobsters. Tirana is very approachable if you're the adventurous type. Crime is rarely, if ever, directed towards foreigners and costs are very low by regional standards. The worst experience you may have i

Public transportation in Tirana consists of a number of intra-city bus lines. A single trip costs 40 lek, there are only single tickets available as of 2023, and tickets are sold in the bus by a conductor. Buses marked Green Line - Unaze number 16B are for the ring road and travel in a loop around the city centre. Thou

Go for a walk in the evening along the main streets or at one of the several parks and sit for a coffee or drink. Take part in the vibrant nightlife by visiting one of the numerous nightclubs.
